Hello Kitty

Yuko Shimizu’s white cat for Sanrio, 1974: a big round head, dot eyes, a yellow nose, a red bow, and no mouth.

Source
Wikipedia: Hello Kitty
Creator
Yuko Shimizu for Sanrio; later lead designers Setsuko Yonekubo (1976) and Yuko Yamaguchi (from 1980)
Made
1974 (first product March 1975)
Style
Kawaii (agent-proposed, not yet reviewed by a person)
Moods
Cute, innocent, sweet
Evidence
Relies on Wikipedia and the V&A’s description of Hello Kitty goods. The 1975 coin purse was not inspected. The character as drawn on later goods was observed on the V&A’s toaster, kettle, and rice cooker.
Reviewed
2 October 2026
Rights
Link and metadata only. License: unverified. Rights policy

Context

Wikipedia says Hello Kitty was designed by Yuko Shimizu and added to Sanrio’s lineup in 1974, and first appeared on an item in March 1975, a vinyl coin purse sold in Japan, sitting between a bottle of milk and a goldfish bowl. Wikipedia: Hello Kitty.

Sanrio describes her as a British anthropomorphic white cat with a red bow and no visible mouth, five apples tall. Setsuko Yonekubo took over as lead designer in 1976; Yuko Yamaguchi has led the design since 1980. Wikipedia: Hello Kitty.

The V&A calls Hello Kitty “the ultimate symbol of Japanese cute”, launched for pre-adolescent girls and now on kettles, toasters, and rice cookers. V&A FE.21-2015.

Observed

  • On the V&A appliances, the head is a wide rounded oval with two pointed ears, outlined in black.
  • The eyes are two black vertical ovals set wide and low; the nose is a small yellow oval; three whiskers sit on each side. No mouth is drawn.
  • A red or pink bow, or a flower, sits at one ear.

Why it belongs

Hello Kitty fixes the kawaii face in its most reduced form. The missing mouth makes the face neutral, so the viewer reads its mood into it.

Because the head works alone as a badge, the character can be put on any product, which is how kawaii spread from stationery to appliances.

Borrow

Design a mascot whose head alone works as an icon at small sizes.

Give the character one signature accessory in one accent color.
